new.readme: One 8 KB skill file that does what REA does: no MCP server, no 207 tools, no setup. The agent then runs the real tools itself.

items.title: Canadian regulated teams gain a two-vendor AWS setup, but residency review becomes the bottleneck
items.connection: GPT models in Canadian Bedrock regions plus strict structured outputs for Claude on Bedrock make vendors swappable behind one schema, while cross-Region routing and Lovable's publish gate move the real work to data review.
items.context: Canadian public sector and health bodies often require data to stay in Canada
chain: Canadian organizations can now call GPT-5.6, GPT-6 and GPT-6.1 on Bedrock from Canada Central and Canada West.
Claude models on Bedrock already support schema-compliant JSON, so a team can hold one output contract and switch vendors per task inside one AWS account.
Cross-Region inference may route data outside the calling region, so the deciding question shifts from model choice to where each call goes.
Lovable admins can block publishing for apps with personal data findings or connectors, giving a natural checkpoint where a residency review can sit before AI-built apps go live.
items.who: Canadian provinces, banks and health agencies benefit; compliance consultancies can sell a residency mapping and go-live review.
items.variable: weeks from prototype to compliance approval
items.versus: Without a defined review step, teams either stall on legal sign-off or ship apps that may send personal data outside Canada.
items.smallest_test: Run one internal workflow on both GPT and Claude via Bedrock under one schema; succeed if both pass schema validation on 99% of 500 calls and every call's processing region is documented.
items.disconfirm: AWS documentation shows these cross-Region calls stay within Canada, removing the need for a separate review.

threats.title: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys compromised
threats.headline: Flawed key generation exposed eMudhra intermediate CA keys, letting attackers impersonate sites to clients outside browsers.
threats.summary: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were incorrectly generated by the CA, so anyone can recover them from the certificates. An attacker with any of these keys could impersonate any website or service. Browsers block the certificates, but many clients outside the browser ecosystem do not consume revocation information or enforce Certificate Transparency.

Test whether your command-line clients still trust the compromised intermediates.

threats.title: uv bundled CA store trusts compromised emSign root
threats.headline: uv's vendored root bundle trusts compromised eMudhra intermediates, exposing uv TLS connections to MITM attacks.
threats.summary: By default, uv verifies TLS connections against a vendored copy of the webpki-root-certs bundle that includes the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root. Eight eMudhra intermediates that chain to that root have compromised private keys. An attacker with one of the keys can issue certificates that uv accepts for any hostname and use them for MITM attacks.
who: Python developers installing packages with uv
threats.quote: An attacker with one of the compromised keys can issue certificates that uv accepts for any hostname, and can be used to issue certificates to enable MITM attacks.

threats.headline: certifi's CA bundle trusts compromised eMudhra intermediates, exposing requests, urllib3 and pip traffic to interception.
threats.summary: An attacker with one of the keys can issue valid-looking certificates for any hostname.
actions: Rebuild container images that vendor certifi.

action_quotes.action: Rebuild container images that vendor certifi.
action_quotes.quote: Upgrade to 2026.10.19 or later, and rebuild container images that vendor certifi.

threats.title: MCP TypeScript client SDK leaks headers on cross-origin redirects
threats.headline: MCP SDK clients followed cross-origin redirects, sending API keys, session IDs and OAuth secrets to other origins.
threats.summary: A server that redirected a request to another origin caused that origin to receive custom request headers, such as an API key, and the mcp-session-id header. On a 307 or 308 the request body also went along, including OAuth token requests with their refresh_token and client_secret.

action_quotes.quote: If a redirect may have reached a host you do not control, rotate the API keys and client_secret your application held and revoke its tokens.

action_quotes.action: Do not restore the old redirect behaviour on transports.
action_quotes.quote: Setting redirectPolicy: 'follow' on a transport restores the old behaviour and the exposure.
